newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh copper plant sees output fall, sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh copper plant sees output fall, sale plan.

text.p: Kazakhstan's troubled Balkhashmys metals plant saw production fall last year and agreed at a board meeting on Tuesday to a state proposal to swap property for state-owned shares in the plant, a company official said.
Erkinbek Shombinov, an acting administrator at Balkhashmys, said the board had approved the scheme, in which the goverment will sell unspecified property through a tender.
A company official who asked not to be named said the plant's output of cathode copper fell to 80,200 tonnes in 1996 from 125,000 tonnes in 1995, according to preliminary figures.

A consortium grouping Glencore AG of Switzerland, Phelps Dodge Corp of the United States and Kazcommerzbank won a tender for an 85 percent state stake in the plant last September in exchange for promises to invest in and manage the enterprise.
No comment was immediately available from the consortium, which had been seeking to sort out the plant's financial situation.

The group had pledged to invest $650 million in the facility by 2005 and to pay off the plant's debt, stated at the tender as totalling $90 million. Some metals sources have the debt could be more than twice that figure.

A member of Balkhashmys's trade union, Amangeldy Taizhanov, said Balkhashmys could eventually be divided into two companies -- one producing copper and the other gold -- and sold through tender or tenders.
Shombinov did not say what property would be sold in exchange for the government stake, whose size he did not name.
"When it's a question of alloting property, it's more attractive to a strategic investor in that it frees him from the obligation of paying the company's debts," he said.
Shombinov also said the board had approved Elkair Syzdykov as president of AO Balkhashmys. He was previously the company's economics director.
The plant, formerly known as Balkhashmed, accounted for about 40 percent of Kazakhstan's copper output in earlier years.
Kazakhstan has the world's third largest copper reserves.
